newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-Taiwan July industry output seen up 4.99 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Taiwan July industry output seen up 4.99 pct.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Tuesday projected an average 4.99 percent year-on-year growth of Taiwan's industrial output in July as floods in southern Taiwan were seen dampening recovering domestic economy.
The official figures are due to be released by the economics ministry at around 0230 GMT on August 21.
Industrial output rose 5.28 percent year-on-year in June. It had risen an average of 6.23 percent year-on-year in January-June period.

Economists said July's industrial output forecast was relatively slow because of floods in south Taiwan.
"The heavy torrential rains in June and early July had slowed industrial output especially in cement and construction industries," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.

But economists said as electronics and information industries were seen to start entering a hot-sale season in July, the industrial output should maintain a stable growth in July and a higher growth in August.

"As electronics and information industries are expected to enter their hot-sale season from July, we can expect a higher growth in August's industrial output," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
